To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the human phosphatidylinositide kinase phosphatidyinositol 4-kiase type III alpha is a modular protein with an N-terminal regulatory module, and that we produced the largest fragment of this module in soluble form in E. coli.
we define a 1100 N-terminal module of human PI4K3A that can be produced and purified in E. coli and that we show that PI4K4a is a two-module protein.

we have defined and expressed soluble fragments of human PIK4A, the N-terminal module of this protein has been expressed and purified to homogeneity, and that PI4KA may be described as a modular protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of large protein fragments in soluble and active form.
the structural and functional characterization of the PI4K4 enzyme family.
the production and purification of large fragments from human PI4KA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PI4KA N-terminus has a regulatory function, but it is still too early to say what this function is.
we have produced the largest N-terminal fragment of PI4KA to date, which is a major step forward towards a structural characterization of this important kinase.

we have shown how to produce and purify a large N-terminal fragment of the human phosphatidylinositide 4-kinases alpha, and that we have also shown how to use a computational approach to delineate the best regions for expression and purification of this protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PI4KA N-terminus is a 1100 residue module with a 300-residue C-terminus that can be described as an intrinsically disordered region (IDR) and a 800-residue region that can be described by secondary structure.
we have been able to express and purify a 1100 residue N-terminal module of PI4K4a, and that this is the first time that a large fragment of PI4K has been expressed in soluble form.
we were able to define and produce in E. coli large fragments of the human lipid kinase PI4KA and to purify the 1100 N-terminal module to homogeneity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PI4KA N-terminus contains a large domain that is not essential to the kinase function of the protein.
computational approaches can help in the design of expression strategies to obtain large protein fragments for structural studies.
computational methods can be successfully used to predict soluble protein fragments from large proteins.
